interpretation: Actual Windows CI exercised all 44 new pure tests within the existing 275-test discovery. The separate 783-test regression was executed locally, not by this Windows workflow. Counts overlap and must not be summed as distinct coverage.

The new modules create no sockets, processes, Jobs, AppContainer profiles, ACLs or firewall rules. They model byte framing, fixed synthetic HTTP, absolute time supplied by a caller, ownership observations and failure behavior only.

Mock READY/DONE and modeled close events do not prove real identity, pipe transport, cleanup or OS enforcement. Successful response observations remain separate from later cleanup failure. The model cannot certify that a future adapter obeys its actions.

The old identity actor was compiled and its downloaded artifact digest matched public metadata. It was not executed; no native bridge binary exists in this slice. Token, Stage0b, restricted and paired runtime steps were skipped.
Genuine target-Windows external inherited-pipe Stage0b remains unproven. Earlier local named-pipe self/child IPC evidence is a different boundary and is not substituted.

The explicit WinHTTP proxy client is cooperative behavior, not proof arbitrary applications cannot bypass a proxy. No proxy-positive, wrong-peer, proxy-death, DNS/broker or product-acceptance runtime result follows.

This commit has no runtime marker and changes no existing source/workflow. Actual proxy identity/capability/peer-policy activation and lifecycle require separately reviewed implementation and a separately authorized bounded run. The pure 10-second model window does not alter existing VM budgets.
